title: Weekly POC: Creds, Gateways, and Infra Readiness
next_steps: Redwood to share updated perf matrix and runbook for KV-cache toggles by 2025-12-19
Devon to confirm VPC peering and return peering route table export by 2025-12-22
Schedule a 30-min security deep-dive with NovaRetail SecOps (Anika + Redwood security SME) week of 2025-12-29
action_items: Maya - send infra checklist + helm values example (link in chat) by EOD 2025-12-17
Liam - re-run the 1k concurrent user benchmark with the reduced batch window and post logs by 2025-12-19
Devon - validate that the subnet used for the pilot has egress to the Redwood public ingress (test id: rgw-88) by 2025-12-22
Anika - provide the list of required compliance docs (SOC2 sections + any additional audit schedules) by 2025-12-20
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on credential handoffs, VPC/gateway routing, and addressing a latency anomaly observed in the 1k-user benchmark. Action items assigned for infra validation, benchmark re-run, and security doc requests.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood here, Liam our SE, and on the NovaRetail side?
[00:08] Sara Lopez (NovaRetail PM): Sara here, hi.
[00:10] Devon Park (NovaRetail Infra): Devon on infra.
[00:12] Anika Rao (NovaRetail Security): Anika from security.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great — planned 45 minutes. I'll kick us off with the agenda: creds status, peering/gateway checks, the benchmark anomaly we saw yesterday, and end with next steps.
[00:30] Liam Patel (Redwood SE): Quick note — I posted the perf dashboard link in the calendar invite and the logs link in the shared drive (see: drive.redwood/example-bench-12-16).
[00:45] Sara: Got it. On creds, we had one issue with the service account permissions — we couldn't write to the KV cash, I mean KV cache, during the warmup.
[00:55] Liam: Right, so that maps to a missing iam:PutObject on the prefix the runtime uses. For the cloud deploy path we require the role to include the RedwoodCacheWrite policy.
[01:08] Devon: We added the role but I think the role was attached to the wrong node pool. We were doing a kube-aws bootstrap and the patch didn't hit the worker nodes.
[01:20] Maya: Ok actionable — Devon can you confirm which node pool is in the helm values? There's an example in the infra checklist I just uploaded — I'll resend.
[01:32] Devon: Yep, please resend. I also want to confirm the V-P-C peering — our infra team sees the peer but the route tables didn't get the propagation.
[01:44] Liam: On the Redwood side we expect two routes: one for the control plane endpoints and one for the inference public ingress. If the routes aren't propagating, the gateway will seem up but packets won't flow.
[01:58] Anika: Security check — are we opening any new ingress from the public internet to our subnets? We want to ensure that the pilot uses the in-region private ingress.
[02:10] Liam: No, by default the pilot uses the private ingress. You only see public ingress if you explicitly enable the public load balancer in the helm values.
[02:22] Sara: That's good. On the benchmark anomaly: yesterday's run hit a latency spike at ~14:12 UTC where p95 jumped from 210ms to 1.8s for about 6 minutes. Logs show a retry burst.
[02:38] Liam: We looked through the logs — two things stood out: a) a small garbage-collection pause on the model worker around that time, and b) an unexpected cache miss rate spike. The miss rate goes from 8% to 63%.
[02:55] Devon: We traced that to a config flip — someone toggled the cache TTL to 0 in the configmap during a test deployment. That would explain the spike.
[03:08] Anika: Was that a human action or automated?
[03:11] Devon: Human. A dev was stress-testing cold starts and accidentally applied the config to the pilot namespace.
[03:18] Maya: Ok good catch. Two parallel items: we can add a guard in the deploy perms so configmaps can't be modified without approval, and we can tune the cache guard so a TTL of 0 is ignored for pilot namespaces.
[03:34] Liam: I'll add a deploy-time validation check in our helm chart that blocks TTL=0 for pilot.* namespaces.
[03:42] Sara: Sounds reasonable. On the creds handoff, we still need SAML SSO mapping for the AE account we created for NovaRetail.
[03:52] Maya: Right — we requested SP metadata earlier. Anika, can you confirm if the Nova IdP team will provide the SAML metadata today?
[03:58] Anika: I can ask but likely next-day. They have a scheduled maintenance today.
[04:04] Maya: Okay we'll plan for tomorrow. Meanwhile we can continue with IAM service account keys for infra-level operations, that's lower risk.
[04:13] Liam: Switching to the gateway routes — Devon, can you paste the output of 'aws ec2 describe-route-tables' for the pilot-route table into the chat? We saw one missing 10.0.5.0/24 entry.
[04:24] Devon: I'm pasting it now in the chat. (link pasted)
[04:30] Liam: Thanks. Yep, missing. That explains the intermittent connectivity. It's likely due to the automated terraform apply that didn't include the new subnet mapping.
[04:41] Devon: Ah, we did run a partial terraform apply yesterday to add a new node pool. That may have overwritten the route attachment.
[04:49] Maya: Noted. Action: Devon to re-run the patch to add the route and confirm with Liam.
[04:56] Sara: Quick question about Dedicated vs Hosted for this pilot: earlier we discussed reserved capacity, but for the pilot we are on shared hosted nodes correct?
[05:06] Liam: Correct — pilot runs on Redwood hosted inference with a tenant-isolated instance. You can opt into Dedicated once you commit to baseline throughput. For now, hosted is faster to iterate on.
[05:20] Sara: Ok. Any risk with data residency? We're required to keep PII within the EU for this pilot.
[05:27] Maya: We're running the pilot in eu-west-1 region per your request. No data leaves the region unless you enable cross-region fallback.
[05:36] Anika: We'll want an attestation of that for our records.
[05:40] Maya: We'll attach the region residency note to the pilot SLA and include the data flow diagram.
[05:46] Liam: Back to the benchmark: I propose we re-run the 1k concurrent user test with a reduced batch window (from 200ms to 50ms) and with KV-cache primed. That should reduce p95 variance.
[05:59] Devon: Sounds good. Curious — how much cost delta do we see when reducing the batch window?
[06:05] Liam: Expect ~7-12% increase in token cost because smaller batches reduce batching efficiency. But you'll trade that for lower tail latency.
[06:15] Sara: That's acceptable while we're validating the UX.
[06:18] Maya: Liam, can you run that test and post the revised numbers?
[06:21] Liam: I'll schedule it for tonight 02:00 UTC and share results in the morning.
[06:26] [07:00] Speaker 5 (Background): mm-hmm
[06:30] [08:00] Sara: One more infra note — our egress firewall blocks outbound to some public subnets by default; we had to whitelist redwood-control.example.com earlier. Is there a list of FQDNs/IP ranges to allow for the pilot?
[06:44] Maya: Yes — I uploaded an allowlist file to the shared drive (redwood/allowlists/pilot-ips.txt). It includes control plane and inference endpoints. I will also paste it in the chat.
[06:55] Devon: Ok I see it. I'll work with NetOps to whitelist.
[07:00] Anika: For compliance, we need to know retention times for logs and request traces. What retention does Redwood keep by default for pilot customers?
[07:09] Liam: Default is 30 days for traces and 90 days for request logs in the hosted plan. We can extend to 365 for enterprise add-on.
[07:18] Anika: We'll want 365 for request logs for auditability, and SOC2 sections related to log integrity.
[07:25] Maya: Noted — that'll be included in the security docs we send.
[07:30] Sara: Back to the anomaly — any chance of an upstream provider blip? We had a minor event from our CDN provider at that timestamp.
[07:38] Liam: We correlated timestamps — the CDN event occurred 2 minutes prior. The model workers actually show the GC pause as the proximate cause, but the CDN event may have amplified client retries.
[07:50] Devon: Do you have suggestions to reduce GC pauses? We're running the default jvm flags on the workers.
[07:56] Liam: We can tune worker heap and GC settings; also move to a slightly larger instance type to reduce CMS pauses. We'll provide recommended flags in the perf doc.
[08:08] Sara: Perfect. Regarding the security deep-dive, can Redwood provide a named security SME?
[08:13] Maya: Yes — I'll introduce you to Priya Shah from Redwood Security. She can cover SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS integration, and the audit logs.
[08:22] Anika: Great. We'll want a Zoom with Priya for 60 minutes. Week of 12/29 works.
[08:30] Maya: Scheduling note captured.
[08:34] [12:00] Liam: Small note on the model variant we used — the team tested with a quantized 8-bit variant. That has slightly higher variance under bursty loads. If you need deterministic p95s, we can pin to 16-bit for the pilot.
[08:50] Devon: Cost implication?
[08:52] Liam: 16-bit roughly 18% more GPU cost per token, but fewer retries and more stable latency.
[08:58] Sara: We'll stick with 8-bit for now and move to 16-bit if the UX requires it.
[09:05] Maya: On the creds handoff again — we created a service account for NovaRetail called nova-pilot-sa; it has limited permissions. Devon, can you confirm you can access the service account keys we shared in the secure bucket?
[09:19] Devon: I see a presigned link but it times out on my side. I might need egress opened to the S3 endpoint.
[09:27] Maya: I'll regenerate a time-extended link for you and post it in the chat.
[09:31] [15:00] Sara: Also, we heard noise about data plane encryption — can you confirm whether payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest when using Redwood hosted?
[09:40] Liam: Yes TLS 1.2+ in transit; at rest we use AES-256 with customer-managed KMS option available for Private/Dedicated. For hosted pilot we can integrate with your KMS via a trust broker — it'll be part of the next steps if you choose the KMS path.
[09:55] Anika: We'll request details on the trust broker flow.
[10:00] Maya: I'll include the KMS diagram and the sequence flows in the security pack.
[10:06] Devon: Quick network test — after I add the route we should also run a traceroute to the control plane to confirm latency.
[10:12] Liam: Agreed. Also, when you rerun the benchmark, please capture the KV hit ratio metric and the GC pause metric. Those two explain most p95 spikes we see.
[10:22] Sara: Liam, can you add thresholds for automatic alerting in the dashboard? Like KV miss > 20% triggers a page.
[10:28] Liam: Yep — I'll add an alert rule and set the default to 25% miss rate and p95 > 500ms. You can customize later.
[10:36] Maya: Any legal/procurement blockers? Sara?
[10:39] Sara: Procurement asked for a draft MSA; we can share a redline but it's not blocking the pilot.
[10:46] Maya: Good. We'll send the pilot MSA template.
[10:50] [20:00] Anika: Regarding audit logs — can Redwood provide immutable logs or do we need a third-party write-once store?
[10:58] Liam: We support append-only logs with retention controls. If you need WORM ledger capabilities we can export to your WORM bucket or an external audit store.
[11:09] Anika: We'll evaluate and get back.
[11:12] Devon: I've kicked the route patch to add 10.0.5.0/24 and will validate after propagation.
[11:18] Sara: Perfect. Anything else on risk?
[11:22] Maya: Two minor risks: accidental config flips (Mitigation: helm guard), and SAML delay (Mitigation: fallback service account keys). Both captured as action items.
[11:34] Liam: I'll also create a runbook step to roll back to the last known config if someone applies TTL=0.
[11:42] Sara: Nice.
[11:46] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps: Maya to send infra checklist and allowlist file; Liam to re-run bench tonight and post logs; Devon to validate peering and route table by 12/22; Anika to gather SAML metadata and security doc list.
[11:58] Anika: I can try to get SAML today but likely by 12/18.
[12:04] Maya: That works. We'll schedule the security deep-dive with Priya for week of 12/29.
[12:10] Devon: I'll confirm once route is propagated and then run traceroute.
[12:16] Liam: I'll upload the updated perf matrix and the KV-cache tuning doc by tomorrow.
[12:22] Sara: Thanks everyone. Quick ask — can we get a concise one-page summary of today and the three immediate items for our C-suite?
[12:30] Maya: Yes — one-pager will be in the follow-up email.
[12:33] [46:00] Maya: All right, thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links and the action item list.
[46:06] End of recording.
